newsitem.title: USA: US lawmaker seeks possible overhaul of FCC.
newsitem.headline: US lawmaker seeks possible overhaul of FCC.

text.p: A key lawmaker Thursday vowed to conduct a major review of the Federal Communications Commission, saying he would seek to overhaul the FCC unless it deregulated the communications markets more aggressively.

"We need to seriously examine the structure of the FCC and perhaps restructure it from the top down," said Rep. Billy Tauzin, a Louisiana Republican who will be the new chairman of the House subcommittee on telecommunications.
He added that among other pieces of legislation his panel will consider is whether to shrink the five-member FCC down to one commissioner, as is the case in the United Kingdom.

Tauzin, in a speech to the Practicing Law Institute and the Federal Communications Bar Association, complained that the FCC was not following the directions stipulated by Congress in implementing this year's telecommunications law.

"The FCC ignored much of what Congress did," Tauzin said, promising that his committee will hold early hearings next year on the FCC's workings and structure. He said the agency had become a "roadblock" to spurring competition.

Among the changes Tauzin said he will consider are: the need for more frequent FCC public hearings; whether to shrink the agency's five commissioners down to one; and whether to have the chairmanship rotate among FCC commissioners, as is now done among state regulatory agencies.

Tauzin also promised to hold hearings on the television ratings system now being completed by TV executives for their programs. And his committee will look at the question of whether the liquor industry should be allowed to advertise on television and radio.
